sub_scenario.family: review and decision quality under interruption density versus protected focused work
sub_scenario.one_line: standards editor: protect a continuous comparison block

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the manuscript queue and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The editorial calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I cleared routine correspondence between meetings without losing track.
Did those messages affect a publication decision?
No, they were routing notes rather than comparative readings.
Someone new shadowed me in the review studio this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the revision weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
I did a standard pass over the editorial calendar records this morning.
Any exceptions in there?
None worth a note.
I discussed a draft with an author for twenty minutes after the section list was settled.
Was that a decision-bearing comparison?
No, it was a clarifying conversation about structure.
I archived last cycle's notes on the editorial calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My review calendar marks protected blocks as unavailable on the shared schedule.
Why make that boundary visible?
A posted block keeps ordinary questions from fragmenting the evidence check.
A vendor call about the manuscript queue ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the review studio checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the revision weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the editorial calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I closed a routine revision weeks cycle without surprises.
Follow-up needed?
A note for the next cycle, nothing more.
I sketched next week's plan for the revision weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the manuscript queue updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The production coordinator holds a 15:00 calendar slot after my review block.
Is that slot fixed?
Yes, it is booked on the editorial calendar.
I compared two options for the editorial calendar tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the review studio handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
How should I handle author questions during tomorrow's policy manuscript review?
